title: Raising Your Family
note: This is the art of raising the family you were born into. It belongs to those who feel shame at falling low, so it follows the chapter on shame.

couplets.plain: Nothing is more dignified than the greatness that says, “I won’t rest my hands from the work.”
couplets.pm: No greatness stands higher than the greatness of effort that says, “I won’t stop the work I began for my family until it is done.” Through many kinds of work the family gains wealth and fame and rises. He rejects “my own work” and “others’ work”: your own work is this work, and doing others’ bidding is no leadership.

links.quote: I won’t rest my hands from the work
links.reason: Sets the refusal to rest your hands from the work above everything else.

links.remove: The couplet doesn’t name the family. He supplies it from the chapter, and the old English wrote it in.

couplets.plain: A family grows through long work that has two things in it: effort and full understanding.
couplets.pm: A man’s family rises through unbroken work that has two things: effort and full knowledge. Knowledge is full when natural sense joins what is learned. Effort keeps laziness out. Full knowledge judges without error which acts will raise you and how to complete them.

couplets.plain: For anyone who says, “I will raise my family,” god tucks up its cloth and goes on ahead.
couplets.pm: For someone who resolves to raise his family and works at what that takes, god ties its garment tight and goes on ahead. Effort is named here by what it brings about. What a person walking in front would do is laid on fate.

links.reason: The mere vow to raise your family sends god on ahead.

couplets.plain: For those who strive without delay for their family, success comes of itself, without planning.
couplets.pm: For those who hurry to the work that serves their family, the way to finish it comes of itself, and they don’t need to plan it. This is the fruit of god going on ahead of them.

links.quote: strive without delay for their family

couplets.plain: The world gathers round a man who raises his family and does no wrong, as if it were his kin.
couplets.pm: The world goes to a man who does no wrong and lives raising his family, and surrounds him, wanting to be his kin. Wrong means acts against righteousness and justice. People draw near him for their own gain too.

links.quote: The world gathers round a man who raises his family

couplets.plain: The good kind of manliness is to make yourself master of the family you were born into.
couplets.pm: What is praised as good manliness in a man is making himself able to rule the family he was born into. “Good” sets this apart from manliness in war. To rule a family is to raise those in it and bring them under your lead.

links.quote: master of the family you were born into
links.reason: Calls being master of the family you were born into the good kind of manliness.

couplets.plain: As the battlefield rests on the fearless, among your own people too the load falls on those who can carry it.
couplets.pm: Many go to the field, but bearing the battle falls to the fearless. Many are born into a family, but bearing its load falls to those able to do it. They are the ones held in high regard.

links.quote: among your own people too the load falls on those who can carry it
the load falls on those who can carry it

couplets.plain: Those raising a family have no season. Be idle and think of your pride, and it is ruined.
couplets.pm: If those raising a family watch the weather, not the work, and also think of their honour, the family falls. So they have no set season. Idleness is saying, “Sun, rain, mist: I’ll do it later.” Honour is saying, “Must I alone suffer while all here are happy?” Rulers at war need the right time. This work doesn’t.

links.quote: Be idle and think of your pride, and it is ruined
Those raising a family have no season

couplets.plain: Is the body of the man who shields his family from harm only a vessel for suffering?
couplets.pm: He works to keep his family from the three kinds of suffering it is open to. Is his body only a vessel for the pain of that effort, and not for joy? The wise man thinks, “If my whole family rises in joy, I gain both worlds, so this bodily pain is good for me,” and never says this, so it is said for him.

couplets.plain: A family with no good person to stand by and prop it up will fall when trouble cuts it at the root.
couplets.pm: A family is a tree. If no good man is born in it, able to give it support and hold it up, it falls with nothing to hold it when the axe of trouble cuts in and fells it at the base. The base is its heirs. It is a tree because it grows and gives fruit with someone to tend it, and dies without.

links.quote: no good person to stand by and prop it up

ideaLinks.quote: A family grows through long work
ideaLinks.reason: Long, unbroken effort is what makes a family grow.
